questions.text: What is 'the controller' that accepts one step forward from a person? Is it a separate service, and how does a person actually trigger a move (button, CLI, flag edit)?

questions.text: The nightly job compares invoices per customer. Which store does it read from, and where does the result (mismatch rate, invoices compared) get written to the rollout record? Who resets or advances the day counts?
questions.about: a nightly job compares the two engines' invoices per customer

questions.about: both --> R1 : manual, or auto when failure rate over 2% in 10 min

questions.text: During R1 to R5 the flag still says both or new_only. What does the new engine do with the flag during that time, and who actually enforces the freeze and holds the queue of due charges?
questions.about: R1 Freeze new-engine charging, queue due charges

questions.text: In R4, where does 'what is due' come from for each customer and period? Which engine or data produces it, especially from new_only where the old engine has been off?
questions.about: R4 Reconcile ledger against due charges

questions.text: What does R3 reprocessing produce, and how is that output used later? The shadow store gets it with no charging, so how does it feed the R5 charges?
questions.about: R3 Old engine reprocesses skipped usage events

questions.text: The diagram has new_only to new_only_locked on 'day 35 reached' with no person, while forward moves need a person. What triggers this transition, and what is day 35 counted from?

From shadow, rollback goes R0 then R5. What does R0 do concretely, and does the old engine need anything at R5 since it was already charging? Also, does the rollback need a person to confirm R5, or does it run straight through each step automatically?
questions.about: R0 Stop new engine, no charges to recover

answers.text: The controller is the rollout controller the brief says will be built; I named it in a new Parts section. It is the only writer of billing_mode, and a person triggers moves with an authenticated admin command to it, not by editing the flag. I chose this so gates and the one-step rule can be enforced in one place. The exact interface (CLI or button) is not decided and not needed yet.

The job reads the shadow store and the ledger (the two engines' invoices sit in those two places in shadow and both). It writes the day's mismatch rate and invoices compared to the rollout record, and the controller advances or resets the day counts and checks gates. Added a Nightly comparison section. Reason: one owner for counters.

The brief does not define charge failure or the denominator. I assumed declined or errored attempts divided by all new-engine charge attempts in the window, measured by the controller from provider responses, but I have no basis to say whether card declines should be excluded. Added to Open questions.

The controller sets a charging frozen switch in the rollout record, and the new engine checks it before every charge; the flag stays unchanged. I dropped the queue of due charges as an extra mechanism: periods that come due while frozen are rediscovered at R4. Reason: simplest handling that still drops nothing.

Due comes from invoices for finished billing periods: the ledger (new engine) plus the shadow store (old engine in both, or R3 reprocessing from new_only), minus periods already charged under the idempotency key at the ledger or provider. R4 and the table now say this.

R3 writes invoices for the skipped usage events into the shadow store. R4 reads them to find periods due, and R5 charges those. Without R3 the new_only gap would have no invoices at all. Stated in R3.

The controller makes this transition by itself, 35 days after the date new_only was entered, which is stored in the rollout record. It is not a forward move, it only closes rollback, so no person is needed. Diagram label and Parts updated.

R0 did nothing concrete, since setting old_only already turns the new engine off and the old engine never stopped charging. I removed R0; from shadow the controller sets billing_mode to old_only directly, and the old engine needs nothing. Rollback steps run automatically one after another with no person confirming R5; stated under the diagram.

questions.text: R3 says the old engine recomputes usage events 'the new engine skipped'. In new_only the new engine does everything, so what does it skip, and how does the old engine know which events those are?
Where is the R4 list of periods due stored, and how does the old engine get it at R5? What happens to a period that comes due after R4 finished but before the flip?
How does the controller find the charges that were 'sent but not confirmed'? Where is that list kept, and what does the new engine do with a charge already in flight when R1 sets the freeze?
What makes a mismatch 'resolved', and who resolves it and records that in the rollout record?

At R5, what happens to the new engine's in-progress work after billing_mode becomes old_only? Does the 'charging frozen' switch stay set until the old engine has started charging, or is it cleared at the same moment as the flip?
What if only a handful of charges happen in a 10-minute window, for example 1 failure out of 3? Does the 2% rule still fire the rollback?
questions.about: New-engine charge failure rate over 2% in any 10-minute window

answers.text: The wording was wrong. In new_only the new engine does everything; it is the old engine that is off. What was skipped is every usage event from the date new_only was entered. That date is in the rollout record, so R3 reprocesses from that date up to the freeze. Reworded R3.

The R4 list is stored in the rollout record. The old engine charges that list first after the flip, then carries on as normal. A period that comes due after R4 is picked up by that normal run; the shared idempotency key stops any double charge. This avoids a second reconcile pass or a lock. Stated in R4 and R5.

Before sending a charge the new engine writes a pending ledger entry under its key, in the same transaction that checks 'charging frozen'. R2 looks up every pending entry at the provider. A charge already sent when R1 sets the freeze is left to finish or stay pending, and R2 settles it. I chose this so the list needs no separate store. Added a Pending charges bullet and updated R1 and R2.

The brief says 'no unresolved mismatches' but does not define resolved or who resolves it. I have no defensible rule. I suggested one option (a person marks it resolved through the controller, or a later nightly run shows it within one cent) but did not build it into the plan. Added to Open questions.

At the flip the new engine turns off, so its in-progress work is dropped; ledger entries it already wrote stay. 'Charging frozen' is cleared after billing_mode is set to old_only, together with the gate counters, so the new engine cannot charge in between and the old engine does not read the switch. Stated in R5.

The brief gives no minimum number of charges. Read literally, 1 failure out of 3 is over 2% and fires the rollback. A minimum attempt count would be a new rule the brief does not require, and I have no basis for its value. Added to Open questions for the owner.

questions.text: The table says the mode does not flip until 'R4 is clean'. What does clean mean here, and who or what decides it?
questions.about: A rollback step fails or times out

questions.text: How does the old engine know it has finished the R4 list, and when is that list cleared from the rollout record? What if the flip happens and the old engine crashes partway through the list?
questions.about: R5 Flip: the old engine charges the R4 list first

questions.text: In R2, if the provider says a pending charge was not charged, does R2 retry it, or does it just record it as not charged and leave it for R4 to find as due?

answers.text: "Clean" was vague wording. It now says the mode does not flip until R4 has finished and stored its list of periods due. The controller decides this: R4 is finished when the list is written to the rollout record. No separate cleanliness check is added. R4 and the failure table now say this.

The old engine removes a period from the R4 list once that period has a charged entry under its key. The list is empty when it is done, so there is no separate clearing step. If the old engine crashes partway, it restarts and continues with what is left on the list. A period already charged is skipped because of the shared idempotency key, so nothing is charged twice. I chose this over a done-flag because the list shrinks on its own and needs no extra state. Stated in R5 and the failure table.

R2 does not retry. If the provider says a pending charge was not charged, R2 only records it as not charged. R4 then finds that period as due, because it has an invoice and no charged entry under its key, and the old engine charges it after the flip. This keeps one place that decides what to charge. Stated in R2 and R4.

teachbacks.text:
I'll follow one scenario: the rollout goes forward to `new_only`, then the new engine starts failing and a rollback runs.

**Forward path**

1. **Start.** A person uses an authenticated admin command to ask the rollout controller to move from `old_only` to `shadow`. The controller is the only thing that writes the `billing_mode` flag, which lives in the config service. It writes `shadow`. No gate applies to this step.
   - In `shadow` the old engine computes, charges and writes the ledger as before.
   - The new engine reads the same usage events and writes its invoices to the shadow store only.
   - Each engine reads `billing_mode` to know what it may do.

2. **Nightly comparison in `shadow`.** A nightly job compares the two engines' invoices per customer. A mismatch is any invoice total that differs by more than one cent.
   - The job writes the day's mismatch rate and the number of invoices compared to the rollout record.
   - The controller owns the counts. It adds a clean day, restarts the count on a bad day, and checks the gate before allowing a move.
   - Gate A is 7 consecutive days with a mismatch rate under 0.1% and at least 5,000 invoices compared. I read the 5,000 as a total over the 7 days, which the document says still needs confirming.
   - A failed or missing nightly job does not count as a pass, and the 7-day count restarts. A mismatch rate of 0.1% or more also restarts the count, with no automatic rollback.
   - New-engine errors in `shadow` are recorded but trigger no rollback. They count only through mismatches.

3. **`shadow` to `both`.** Once gate A is met, a person asks the controller to move forward. The controller accepts one step forward from a person only. Skipping a step, or moving forward without a person, is rejected. The controller sets `billing_mode` to `both`.
   - The old engine now computes every invoice into the shadow store, with no charges.
   - The new engine computes, charges and writes the ledger.
   - The nightly job keeps comparing. It reads the shadow store (old engine's invoices) and the ledger (new engine's invoices).

4. **How a new-engine charge works in `both` or `new_only`.**
   - Each charge has one idempotency key per customer and billing period. The ledger and the payment provider both use it, and both engines use the same key.
   - Before sending a charge, the new engine writes a "pending" ledger entry under that key. It does this in the same ledger transaction that checks the "charging frozen" switch in the rollout record.
   - When the provider answers, the entry becomes charged or not charged.

5. **`both` to `new_only`.** This needs gate B and Finance sign-off.
   - Gate B is 14 days in `both` with no unresolved mismatches.
   - An unresolved mismatch keeps the rollout in `both`. Missing Finance sign-off blocks the move.
   - When both are satisfied, a person asks and the controller sets `new_only`. The old engine stops computing and the new engine does everything. The controller records the date `new_only` was entered in the rollout record.

6. **Day 35.** The controller moves `new_only` to `new_only_locked` 35 days after `new_only` was entered. No rollback is possible from there. A rollback trigger on day 35 or later does not roll back. It pages on-call, who fix forward. Later, a person can move to `decommissioned`, which removes the old engine.

**Failure and rollback**

7. **Trigger.** In `both` or `new_only`, the controller measures the new engine's charge failure rate from the provider's responses. If it is over 2% in any 10-minute window, the controller starts a rollback at R1 and pages on-call. On-call can also start a rollback by hand from `shadow`, `both` or `new_only`, and that follows the same path. Only one rollback is active at a time. A second trigger, such as the alarm firing again, joins the active rollback.

8. **R1 Freeze.** The controller sets "charging frozen" in the rollout record. The new engine checks it before every charge and sends none. A charge already sent is left to finish or stay pending. The `billing_mode` flag keeps its old value. Nothing is queued. Periods that come due while frozen are found again at R4.

9. **R2 Settle.** Every "pending" ledger entry is looked up at the payment provider by its key. Each ends as charged or not charged.
   - R2 does not retry a "not charged" result. It only records it, and R4 will find that period as due.
   - If an outcome is unknown, it is treated as unresolved. The controller queries the provider again and never re-charges until the provider says the charge did not happen.

10. **R3 Reprocess (only if the rollback began in `new_only`).** The old engine was off from the date `new_only` was entered. The old engine recomputes the usage events from that date up to the freeze into the shadow store, with no charging. This produces invoices that exist nowhere else. From `both`, R3 is skipped because the old engine already wrote its invoices to the shadow store.

11. **R4 Reconcile.** The controller takes every invoice for a finished billing period from the ledger (written by the new engine) and from the shadow store (written by the old engine in `both`, or by R3).
    - A period is due when it has an invoice and no charged entry under its key at the ledger or the provider. A "not charged" entry counts as no charge.
    - The result is stored in the rollout record as the list of periods due and not yet charged. R4 is finished once that list is stored.

12. **R5 Flip.** The controller sets `billing_mode` to `old_only`. The new engine is now off, and any work it had in progress is dropped. Ledger entries it already wrote stay. Then the controller clears all gate counters, the Finance sign-off and "charging frozen". The 7-day count goes back to 0. The rollout must go through `shadow` again.
    - The old engine resumes charging. It charges the R4 list first, then carries on as normal.
    - It removes a period from the list once that period has a charged entry. The list is empty when it is done.
    - Periods that come due after R4 are charged by the normal run. The shared key stops any period being charged twice.
    - If the old engine crashes partway, it restarts and continues with what is left on the list.

13. **Rollback from `shadow`.** The new engine never charged and the old engine never stopped. The controller only sets `billing_mode` to `old_only`, which also turns the new engine off. It skips R1 to R4.

14. **If a rollback step fails or times out.** The rollback stays at that step and retries, and on-call is paged. The mode does not flip until R4 has stored its list. Charging stays frozen meanwhile, so customers may be billed late but not twice. Rollback steps run one after another without a person confirming each one. A person only starts a manual rollback and answers pages.
gaps: The document does not say how the nightly job gets its identity or schedule, or how it reports to the rollout record. It only says the job writes the day's rate and invoice count there.

The document does not say how the new engine and the old engine learn that `billing_mode` or `charging frozen` has changed. It does not say whether they poll or are notified. This matters because the new engine checks 'charging frozen' inside the ledger transaction, while the flag lives in the config service.
Mismatch 'resolved' is undefined, so I cannot say what moves gate B from unmet to met in `both`. The document lists this as an open question.

The document does not define the charge failure rate. It does not say whether card declines count, or what happens with very few charges in a window. So I cannot say exactly when the automatic rollback trigger fires. These are listed as open questions.
The document does not say how the controller detects that a rollback step has failed or timed out, what the timeout values are, or how many retries happen.

The document does not say how a period gets from 'due' to 'charged' on the old engine at R5 beyond 'it charges the list'. It also does not say how the old engine reads the R4 list from the rollout record.
It is unclear whether new-engine charges still in flight at R5 (sent before the freeze but not settled) are covered. R5 says in-progress work is dropped, and R2 only settles entries marked pending.

The document does not say what happens to a rollback already in progress when day 35 arrives, or whether a rollback can start at day 34 without losing usage events before R3 finishes. This is an open question.
The document says the controller can only be driven by an authenticated admin command, but not how the identity or authorization works, or what the command looks like.
The document says the rollout record sits in the ledger's database only as an assumption, so where it really lives is unconfirmed.
